title: Multiplayer Lens Optics Demo
prompt:
Create an interactive Three.js educational demo simulating thin lens optics with two independent player viewports (split-screen). The HTML file must include everything inline.

## Scene Setup
- Use two THREE.WebGLRenderer instances or a single renderer with scissor/viewport for a LEFT (Player 1) and RIGHT (Player 2) split-screen, each 50% of window width.
- Each viewport has its own OrthographicCamera looking down the Z-axis at a 2D optics bench.
- Background color: #1a1a2e for both viewports.
- Add a horizontal principal axis (white dashed line) spanning the full width of each viewport at y=0.
- Place a vertical thin convex lens (cyan colored, drawn as a double-arrow shape or bi-convex outline) at x=0 in each viewport.
- The lens has a default focal length f=3 units.
- Place an upright arrow (the 'object') colored RED for Player 1 (left viewport) and GREEN for Player 2 (right viewport) at initial positions: Player 1 object at x=-8, Player 2 object at x=-6. Object height = 2 units.
- Compute and render the IMAGE arrow using the thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, where do = |object_x| (positive, object is on left of lens). Image position di is computed, and magnification m = -di/do. The image arrow should be BLUE for P1 and YELLOW for P2, rendered at x=di with height = m * object_height. If the image is virtual (di < 0), draw it as a dashed/translucent arrow on the same side as the object.
- Draw 3 principal rays from the tip of each object arrow through the lens to the image tip: (1) parallel to axis, refracts through far focal point; (2) through the near focal point, refracts parallel; (3) through the lens center, undeviated. Color rays to match the object color with some transparency.

## UI Elements
- A top HUD bar showing: 'Player 1: do=X.XX, di=X.XX, m=X.XX | Player 2: do=X.XX, di=X.XX, m=X.XX'
- A dropdown (id='lensType') with options: 'Convex' (f>0) and 'Concave' (f<0, use f=-3). Changing this updates BOTH viewports.
- A slider (id='focalSlider') range 1.0 to 8.0, step 0.1, default 3.0, controlling |f| (sign from lensType). Label it 'Focal Length: X.X'.
- A button (id='resetBtn') labeled 'Reset All' that resets objects to initial positions, lens to convex, f=3.
- A button (id='swapBtn') labeled 'Swap Objects' that swaps Player 1 and Player 2 object x-positions.

## Interactions
- Player 1 moves their object with keys A (left, decrease do) and D (right, increase do toward lens), clamped to x in [-12, -0.5].
- Player 2 moves their object with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, same clamp range.
- Each key press moves the object by 0.5 units.
- All ray diagrams, image arrows, and HUD update in real-time on every change.
- Focal point markers (small circles or diamonds) should be visible on the axis at x=+f and x=-f.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- p1_do: (positive number) Player 1 object distance from lens (absolute value)
- p1_di: (number) Player 1 image distance (positive=real, negative=virtual)
- p1_mag: (number) magnification for Player 1
- p1_obj_x: (number) Player 1 object x position (negative)
- p2_do: (positive number) Player 2 object distance
- p2_di: (number) Player 2 image distance
- p2_mag: (number) Player 2 magnification
- p2_obj_x: (number) Player 2 object x position (negative)
- focal_length: (number) current focal length with sign
- lens_type: (string) 'convex' or 'concave'
- p1_image_real: (boolean) true if Player 1 image is real
- p2_image_real: (boolean) true if Player 2 image is real
- ray_count_p1: (number) number of principal rays drawn for P1 (should be 3)
- ray_count_p2: (number) number of principal rays drawn for P2 (should be 3)
- p1_image_height: (number) height of P1 image arrow
- p2_image_height: (number) height of P2 image arrow

## Physics Constraints
- Thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di must hold precisely.
- Magnification: m = -di/do.
- Image height = |m| * object_height, inverted if m < 0.
- For convex lens with do > f: real inverted image. For do < f: virtual upright image.
- For concave lens: always virtual upright image.
- No NaN values in any state field.
physics_constraints: Thin lens equation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di must hold at all times. Magnification m = -di/do. Image is real when di > 0, virtual when di < 0. Convex lens f > 0, concave lens f < 0. Object distance do must always be positive.
